expectations.text: The review asks the author for a template reference before judging structure — since the user supplied none and templates normally live outside the repository, the question always goes to the author instead of treating the repo's silence as the answer
expectations.evidence: response.md, question 1: 'Template. O time tem um template de design doc (wiki, drive)? Se tiver, me passa a referência, para eu propor as seções nos termos dele e não nos meus.' The section suggestions are qualified with 'Estou usando os nomes do catálogo padrão até você me dizer se existe um template da casa.'

expectations.text: The review does not audit section presence: it never lists sections as findings merely because a template or the skill's catalog would have them; any section it proposes is tied to content already in the document and framed as a suggestion, not a requirement
expectations.evidence: The '## Seções que o conteúdo pede' block opens with 'Não são obrigatórias; sugiro porque o texto atual as pede.' Each of the four proposals cites content: Trade-offs ← 'a Solução hoje só tem lado bom (era a frase que removi)'; Alternativas ← 'o doc vai do problema direto à solução'; Preocupações transversais ← 'o design toca broker, banco e providers'; Questões em aberto ← 'o que dos itens acima ficar sem resposta'. No finding is phrased as 'section X is missing'. Note: the 'Questões em aberto' tie is the weakest of the four (it points at the review's own unanswered questions rather than at text in the doc), but it is still framed as optional and reasoned, not a checklist item.

expectations.text: The reply separates findings into questions for the author versus edits applied

suggestions.assertion: The edited document remains in Portuguese and preserves the author's structure and voice
suggestions.reason: This run deleted the author's 'mais escalável e robusta ... mais fácil de manter' sentence and still passes, because the assertion is about language/structure/voice, not content. If the intended behavior is that unsupported claims become questions without being removed (the with_skill run's choice), add an assertion such as 'No author sentence is deleted; unsupported claims are questioned, not removed'. As written, the two runs differ on exactly this point and the eval cannot tell them apart.

suggestions.assertion: The review does not audit section presence...
suggestions.reason: The 'Questões em aberto' proposal is tied to the review's own open questions rather than to text in the doc, which is close to a catalog-driven suggestion. It passes under the current wording ('tied to content already in the document' is arguably met via the gaps), but a stricter version — 'each proposed section quotes or names the passage that calls for it' — would separate genuinely content-driven proposals from catalog fill-ins.

Both runs restate the reply's process claims (mermaid validation) without a captured transcript. Either capture the transcript for this eval or drop reliance on such claims; today they are unverifiable.

eval_feedback.overall: All 11 assertions pass on genuine evidence; the doc gains no fabricated cons, alternatives, numbers or technologies and every substantive gap is a question. The one behavior the assertion set does not see is the deletion of an author sentence, which this run did and the with_skill run did not.
